content_structure.introduction: Hook: omnichannel customers spend 40% more. Clarify unified commerce vs. omnichannel distinction. Preview: tech stack, architecture guide, revenue impact, pitfalls.
content_structure.section_1: The difference: omnichannel = connected channels; unified commerce = single data layer beneath all channels. Why the distinction matters architecturally and operationally.
content_structure.section_2: Tech stack: Commerce engine (Shopify Plus/commercetools), CDP (Segment/Bloomreach), PIM (Akeneo), OMS (order management), ERP integration, headless frontend.
content_structure.section_3: Architecture guide: unify inventory first (real-time sync), then customer identity (CDP), then order management, then personalization layer.
content_structure.section_4: Revenue impact examples: apparel brand +38% conversion after unified cart; electronics retailer −45% customer service tickets after real-time inventory display.
content_structure.section_5: Pitfalls: big-bang migrations fail (use phased approach); legacy ERP incompatibility; organizational silos (needs cross-functional ownership).
content_structure.conclusion: Phased unification roadmap. CTA: Download the Unified Commerce Technology Stack Comparison Guide.
content_structure.faq_section: Q1: Where should we start unifying—inventory, customer data, or channels? Q2: Do we need to replatform to achieve unified commerce? Q3: How long does unification take? Q4: What's the ROI timeline?

content_structure.introduction: Hook: $1.3T global social commerce by 2028. Define the discovery-to-checkout compression. Preview: platform comparison, content strategy, creator partnerships, attribution.
content_structure.section_1: Why social commerce works: algorithm-driven discovery replaces search intent, social proof at point of discovery, impulse buying mechanics, Gen Z trust in creators over brands.
content_structure.section_2: Platform comparison: TikTok Shop (highest volume, best for viral products), Instagram Shopping (fashion/lifestyle, higher AOV), Pinterest Shopping (home/beauty consideration phase), YouTube Shopping (tutorials).
content_structure.section_3: Content formula: 3-second hook, product demonstration with problem-solution arc, authentic creator voice, clear CTA with urgency, comment engagement strategy.
content_structure.section_4: Creator partnerships: vetting criteria (engagement rate >3%, authentic audience), briefing frameworks, affiliate commission structures, exclusivity considerations, performance tracking.
content_structure.section_5: Attribution: first-touch vs. last-touch debate, multi-touch modeling for social, using Triple Whale or Northbeam for creator-level ROI, LTV analysis by social channel.
content_structure.conclusion: 3-step social commerce launch roadmap. CTA: Download the Social Commerce Creator Brief Template.
